title: Who Walks for Water? Water Consumption and Labor Supply Response to Rainfall Scarcity in Uganda
abstract: This paper examines how rainfall scarcity affects water collection and labor supply in Uganda. It combines a nationally representative household panel with satellite-based rainfall measures to study the consequences of drought for household water use and work. Scarcity increases the time required to collect water and changes labor-supply decisions, with women and girls carrying a disproportionate share of the collection burden. The findings show how climate shocks can affect economic activity through the time households must devote to obtaining essential resources.
